Hi Emma — great to hear and thanks for the SOW.

Overview: we've sketched a condensed MAP below with the items you listed. This is a working timeline — we've kept the POC to a 10 business-day runway with clear ownership. Please review and confirm dates that work for your procurement and infra teams.

Mutual action plan (high level):
- Day 0 (prep): BioMedAI provides contact for procurement and infra, desired tenant name, and initial CIDRs.
- Day 1: Redwood creates org + staging tenant; generate scoped API keys for POC (test-only).
- Day 2-3: IP allowlist applied; test connectivity to staging endpoints.
- Day 4-6: VPC peering request + routing verification (canary routing for small traffic).
- Day 7-10: Load test, latency baseline, joint validation; sign-off on success criteria.

Open items / risks:
- If your security team requires cross-account peering with strict egress rules, that can add 2-4 days.
- Dedicated on-prem routing or manual firewall approvals will push timeline depending on your change window.

What we need from you today:
1) Tenant/org name to create (format we recommend: biomedai-poc-2026).
2) CIDR(s) for allowlist + preferred peering subnet suggestions.
3) Primary procurement contact and PO timeline.

I'll loop in Olga (technical lead) below to call out the peering checklist. Attached is a short MAP draft (map-draft.docx) linking to our onboarding doc.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m sync if you prefer to run the timeline together.

Best,
Jonas Weber

Emma — tagging in a few technical details on the VPC peering and IP allowlist to avoid surprises: 

VPC peering checklist (what we need from BioMedAI):
- Your VPC ID and AWS account number (or GCP project + VPC name).
- Peering CIDR: preferred /24 or /26 ranges we can route to for the POC. Avoid overlapping CIDRs with Redwood staging (we will share ours).
- Public egress IP(s) to allow for callbacks to our management API (if you cannot NAT, share the instances that will initiate outbound).
- Any firewall appliance in the path that requires a change window.

IP allowlist guidance:
- For fastest onboarding provide a short list (e.g., two /28 or one /24) for the POC. We recommend the POC allowlist be time-bound (we'll expire keys + remove IPs after sign-off).

API key scoping / RBAC:
- We can create API keys scoped to: read-only (embeddings/queries) or full write (generation). For safety we typically provision a scoped key for initial runs and rotate to broader keys only after validation.
- Org setup: we recommend creating two roles: engineers (read/write to staging) and ops (admin + peering approvals). We'll provide a template.

Potential constraints:
- If your security requires HSM-backed key wrapping for every API key, we will need to coordinate with our account security team (adds 3-5 business days).

I'll send our peering template and sample CIDRs later today. If you can share the VPC/account details, we'll kick off the peering request immediately.

—Olga
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood
